passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: INTRODUCTION TO MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS The purpose of this section, Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (“MD&A”), is to provide a narrative explanation of our financial statements that enables investors to better understand our business, to enhance our overall financial disclosures, to give context to the analysis of our financial information, and to provide information about the quality of, and potential variability of, our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows. MD&A, which should be read in conjunction with the accompanying Consolidated Financial Statements, includes the following sections: • Management Overview • Sources of Revenue for Our Hospital Operations and Services Segment • Results of Operations • Liquidity and Capital Resources • Recently Issued Accounting Standards • Critical Accounting Estimates Our business consists of our Hospital Operations and Services (“Hospital Operations”) segment and our Ambulatory Care segment. Our Hospital Operations segment is comprised of our acute care and specialty hospitals, a network of employed physicians and ancillary outpatient facilities. At December 31, 2025, our subsidiaries operated 50 hospitals serving primarily urban and suburban communities in eight states. Our Hospital Operations segment also included 132 outpatient facilities, namely urgent care centers, imaging centers, off-campus hospital emergency departments and micro‑hospitals, at December 31, 2025. In addition, our Hospital Operations segment provides revenue cycle management and value‑based care services to hospitals, health systems, physician practices, employers and other clients through Conifer Health Solutions, LLC. Our Ambulatory Care segment, through USPI Holding Company, Inc. (together with its subsidiaries, “USPI”), held ownership interests in 533 ambulatory surgery centers (each, an “ASC”), 401 of which are consolidated, and 26 surgical hospitals, eight of which are consolidated, in 37 states at December 31, 2025. USPI’s facilities offer a range of procedures and service lines, including, among other specialties: orthopedics, total joint replacement, and spinal and other musculoskeletal procedures; gastroenterology; pain management; otolaryngology (ear, nose and throat); ophthalmology; and urology. Unless otherwise indicated, all financial and statistical information included in MD&A relates to our continuing operations, with dollar amounts expressed in millions (except per adjusted admission and per adjusted patient day amounts). Continuing operations information includes the results of all facilities operated during any portion of the periods presented, and it reflects the performance of those facilities only for the time periods in which we operated them. Continuing operations information excludes the results of our hospitals and other businesses classified as discontinued operations for accounting purposes. We believe this presentation is useful to investors because continuing operations information reflects the impact of the addition or disposition of individual hospitals and other operations on our volumes, revenues and expenses.

passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Our business is subject to a number of risks and uncertainties, many of which are beyond our control, that may cause our actual operating results or financial performance to be materially different from our expectations and make an investment in our securities risky. The disclosures in this section reflect our beliefs and opinions as to factors that could materially and adversely affect us in the future. References to past events are provided by way of example only and are not intended to be a complete listing or a representation as to whether or not such factors have occurred in the past. If one or more of the events discussed in this report were to occur, actual outcomes could differ materially from those expressed in or implied by any forward‑looking statements we make in this report or our other filings with the SEC, and our business, financial condition, results of operations or liquidity could be materially adversely affected; furthermore, the trading price of our common stock could decline and our shareholders could lose all or part of their investment. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known, or currently deemed immaterial, may also constrain our business and operations. Risks Related to Our Overall Operations If we are unable to enter into, maintain and renew managed care contractual arrangements on competitive terms, if we experience material reductions in the contracted rates we receive from managed care payers or if we have difficulty collecting from managed care payers, our results of operations could be adversely affected. Our ability to enter into, maintain and renew favorable contracts with HMOs, insurers offering preferred provider arrangements and other managed care plans, as well as add new facilities to our existing agreements at contracted rates, significantly affects our revenues and operating results. For the year ended December 31, 2025, approximately 70%, or $9.696 billion, of our net patient service revenues for the hospitals and related outpatient facilities in our Hospital Operations segment was attributable to managed care payers, including Medicare and Medicaid managed care programs. The ongoing trend toward consolidation among non‑government payers tends to increase their bargaining power over contract terms. Generally, we compete for these contracts on the basis of price, market reputation, geographic location, quality and range of services, caliber of the medical staff and convenience. If we are unable to negotiate increased reimbursement rates, maintain existing rates or other favorable contract terms, effectively respond to managed care payer cost controls and reimbursement policies, or comply with the terms of our contracts, the payments we receive for our services may be reduced. Also, in recent years, we have increasingly experienced payment denials from and other administrative challenges with managed care payers, both prospectively and retroactively. We currently have thousands of managed care contracts with various HMOs and PPOs; however, our top 10 managed care payers generated 69% of our managed care net patient service revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow comfortably exceeds share repurchases, so internal cash generation funds the buyback programme with room to spare; this supports the intermediate cash-flow tier and gives management flexibility to reduce debt or absorb volume softness without external funding.

Free cash flow covers buybacks by a clear margin, and free cash flow to debt improved materially year over year, indicating stronger deleveraging capacity than the prior period despite the absolute leverage level remaining elevated relative to peers.

key_risks.text: Managed care concentration is the central revenue risk: the top ten payers dominate managed care net patient service revenue, and payer consolidation plus rising payment denials could compress reimbursement and delay collections across the hospital portfolio.

The debt stack is large and laddered from near-term first lien maturities through later unsecured notes; the issuer has actively refinanced, extending maturities and redeeming second lien notes, but refinancing execution and fixed-rate coupon burden remain material to the credit profile.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage sits below the sector median and fell sharply year over year, while EBITDA coverage is also below peers; the operating margin contracted versus the prior year and trails the sector median, so debt service headroom depends on restoring earnings.

Gross and net leverage both sit above sector medians and rose year over year, though net leverage remains below the next risk-band boundary; cash flow to debt is below the peer median but above the downgrade threshold, leaving modest cushion.

overall_credit_view.text: The issuer is a large acute-care and ambulatory surgery operator with a diversified facility footprint and solid cash generation; the indicative financial risk profile is intermediate, with leverage above sector medians and coverage below them, while cash flow metrics improved year over year.

Our forward view is that credit quality hinges on managed care contract renewals and margin recovery; continued buybacks absorb free cash flow, so deleveraging is likely gradual, and refinancing of the laddered note maturities will be the key test of market access.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流穩健地超過股份回購，因此內部現金產生足以資助回購計劃且有餘裕；這支持中間現金流級別，並給予管理層靈活性以減少債務或吸收業務量疲軟而無需外部融資。
自由現金流以明顯幅度覆蓋回購，且自由現金流對債務比率較去年同期大幅改善，表明儘管絕對槓桿水平相對同業仍偏高，去槓桿能力較前期更強。

key_risks.text: 管理式醫療集中度是核心收入風險：前十大付款方主導管理式醫療淨病人服務收入，而付款方整合加上日益增加的付款拒付可能壓縮報銷並延遲整個醫院組合的收款。
債務結構龐大且從近期第一留置權到期日至較後無擔保票據呈階梯式分佈；發行人已積極再融資，延長到期日並贖回第二留置權票據，但再融資執行及固定利率票息負擔對信用狀況仍屬重大。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率低於行業中位數且較去年同期大幅下降，而EBITDA覆蓋率亦低於同業；營業利潤率較去年收縮並落後於行業中位數，因此償債空間取決於盈利恢復。
總槓桿及淨槓桿均高於行業中位數且較去年同期上升，儘管淨槓桿仍低於下一風險區間邊界；現金流對債務比率低於同業中位數但高於降級門檻，留有溫和緩衝。

overall_credit_view.text: 發行人是一家大型急症護理及門診手術營運商，擁有多元化設施佈局及穩健現金產生；指示性財務風險狀況為中間，槓桿高於行業中位數而覆蓋率低於中位數，同時現金流指標較去年同期改善。
我們的前瞻觀點是信用質量取決於管理式醫療合約續約及利潤率恢復；持續回購吸收自由現金流，因此去槓桿可能漸進，而階梯式票據到期的再融資將是市場準入的關鍵考驗。
